assets.description: Active Pi session identity, transcript and queue
Task journal, control revision and dispatch authority
Approval decisions, nonces and exact action preconditions
Workspace source, protected paths and Git index
Task baseline, provenance, verifier and handoff evidence
Credentials, tokens and sensitive tool or log output
Pi terminal execution and local machine resources
Static WebUI bundle and pinned dependency integrity
Browser-selected staged attachment bytes and one-shot dispatch references
Gateway and terminal owner epochs, runtime leases and session admission
Durable session command intent, idempotency and crash ambiguity evidence

controls.requirement: Bind only 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port; expose no host or LAN option.
Validate exact Host and Origin and emit no wildcard CORS response.
Use a 256-bit per-launch fragment capability, one-time exchange and HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie.
Require authenticated cookie, exact Origin and CSRF token on every side-effect request.
Ship local static assets with strict CSP, no eval, remote asset, frame, object, base or service worker authority.
Render filenames, diffs, logs, tool arguments and model text as escaped text; strip ANSI and control characters.
Bind snapshot, event and request to exact project, runtime, session, task, operation and revision where available.
Use the current Pi process bridge; never attach by starting or owning a second Pi runtime.
Browser and sidecar emit typed intents only; Pi guard is the sole action executor and policy authority.

Bind one-time approval nonce to runtime/session/task/operation/tool/keyed-action-commitment/revision with expiry and first-valid CAS; allow creates only a provisional permit that the guard rechecks and consumes immediately before tool start.
Accept only server-issued opaque refs; canonicalize below fixed Git roots and reject traversal or symlink escape.
Apply the effective protected-path policy before content, diff or log material enters a browser response.
Use argv-only read commands, sanitized environment, no hooks, pager, external diff, textconv or submodule recursion.
Keep bounded evidence owner-only, exclude protected content, use no workspace Git object, and fail closed on corruption.
Project unavailable, mixed or unattributed facts rather than infer provenance, verifier, running or completion state.
Bound request bytes, collections, replay, diff, log, process concurrency, time and client count; cancel abandoned work.
Reuse guard redaction before persistence and response; expose opaque refs instead of secret-bearing raw paths.
Sidecar/UI crash, disk failure or corrupt projection cannot interrupt Pi task, terminal, tool or verifier execution.
Use a minimal pinned local bundle with package allowlist, no CDN, analytics, runtime plugin or dynamic code loader.
Accept browser-selected bytes only; verify MIME and limits, store owner-only, bind opaque one-shot refs to runtime/session/message/expiry, and make stage/discard zero-turn.

Recompute the exact selected source view/file/diff in Pi, bind review to task/workspace/index/view/file revisions and patch preimage, reject incomplete content, and persist only bounded opaque digest evidence.

Require an exact-session Pi guard binding, resolve one opaque file target and any canonical ordered opaque hunk selection in the guard, bind selected workspace and whole-index preimages, derive bounded raw patch bytes only inside the runtime, acquire an owned exclusive index lock, build a private temporary index with fixed no-filter Git argv, recheck authority before atomic replace, and persist bounded requested/terminal evidence without patch text.

Expose a bounded exact index-to-working-tree text preview, require an explicit expiring confirmation HMAC-bound by a per-runtime secret never projected to the browser, allow only exact runtime provenance and one ordinary unprotected path, recheck task/control/index/workspace authority under an owned path lock, restore only the selected file or one hunk while preserving the index, and persist no source or patch text.

Accept only one opaque current-file reference and bounded location, resolve an ordinary unprotected regular file below exact project and Git roots, launch only a verified Visual Studio Code CLI with fixed no-shell argv, provide no Cursor or generic launcher fallback, and persist only path-free idempotency evidence.

Derive deterministic advisory text only from the exact bounded staged projection with no source reads or model turn, omit protected names, and require a separate pre-dispatch token warning before one ordinary same-session Pi chat operation can rewrite it.

Require every Stage, Unstage and Revert receipt to resolve to a durable owner-only requested/terminal audit chain, invalidate index-bound review state on index mutation, preserve verifier currency when working-tree bytes are unchanged, and derive Revert review/verifier staleness only from exact current digests and verifier file snapshots.

Project a maximum of 200 recent task runs only from validated Task Contract and session binding state, preserve exact task/run identity, omit raw session IDs and state filenames, redact display metadata, expose corrupt/legacy/truncated input only as bounded warning counts, and provide no task mutation or model-work path.

Project at most 300 exact task/run/session events only from a hash- and sequence-valid Task Journal, expose fixed event classes and bounded redacted details through opaque run refs, fail closed on corruption, label an incomplete tail only as possible interruption, keep missing explicit crash evidence unknown, and provide no replay, control, continuation or model-work path.

Project at most 300 exact task/run/session compaction metadata facts from bounded local telemetry plus the existing recovery projector, redact display fields, expose only opaque evidence refs, never expose capture paths, content hashes, inputs, raw retained bodies or session IDs, label corrupt, incomplete, missing and truncated telemetry explicitly, and provide no compaction trigger, recovery replay, continuation or model-work path.

Project at most 100 exact task/run/session handoff-write facts from bounded telemetry, bind the latest validated handoff projection and existing resume-state next action to that run, expose only fixed bounded summaries and opaque refs, fail closed on an invalid latest handoff, label snapshot-only, missing, corrupt, incomplete and truncated history explicitly, and never expose raw state paths, handoff bodies, session IDs, verifier commands or an executable next-action endpoint.

Project at most 64 direct helper children only from the exact validated task/run owned-work ledger and bounded acceptance helper receipts, derive expired leases as orphaned without mutating runtime state, expose opaque node refs, fixed role/authority/lifecycle/result facts and current writer ownership, reject corrupt ledgers, label missing ledgers and unavailable nested lineage explicitly, and never expose helper prompts, outputs, models, session identity, reservation IDs, request digests or output digests.

Project at most 20 benchmark summaries only from report-to-ledger-bound local evidence associated with the current repository, bind release readiness to the exact Git head and candidate content digest, mark historical evidence stale, reject corrupt or cross-project input, redact display metadata, expose only opaque refs, and advertise every benchmark and release mutation as unavailable.

Keep every long-task projection within fixed record, byte and response ceilings; preserve deterministic revisions over the newest retained window; label truncated or missing history explicitly; and fail closed without reading through symlinks or trusting oversized, replaced, corrupt or cross-run evidence.

Run exactly one owner-only local Gateway per canonical Pi profile, reject duplicate daemon admission, bind descriptors, IPC and state to the exact profile, and settle or mark every command uncertain before an explicit stop.

Acquire one random owner epoch by atomic session admission before creating a Pi runtime, challenge active owners over their exact channel, reject PID-only liveness and never steal an owner when liveness, profile, session stability or lease continuity is unknown.

Register terminal ownership before catalog availability and consume a one-time release only after idle, no pending operation or approval, durable session flush and terminal no-further-write acknowledgement; reject old-epoch reconnects and never infer release from Gateway restart.

Persist and fsync bounded create, send and fork intent before Pi effect, carry exact idempotency and revision bindings through prepared, dispatched and terminal states, never auto-replay an ambiguous dispatched command, and keep any pending raw content private, no-follow and absent from browser hashes or logs.

Issue a new Gateway and browser authority after restart, default-deny pending approvals, revalidate every owner before opening a runtime, and reconcile missing first-assistant session files or fork paths only against the admission journal while presenting unproven effects as recovery-required or uncertain.

Build a bounded catalog only from validated Pi session metadata and Gateway overlay state, redact every display field, expose opaque references instead of raw session IDs or local paths, and keep offline list, search, pin and archive projection free of runtime acquisition and provider calls.

threats.attack: Another local or LAN principal reaches an unauthenticated server.
threats.residualRisk: Processes under the same OS account remain outside application isolation.

threats.attack: A hostile origin or DNS rebinding page drives localhost endpoints.
threats.residualRisk: A fully compromised browser profile can act with the operator's browser authority.

threats.attack: Repository, diff, log or model text executes script and steals approval authority.
threats.residualRisk: Browser engine vulnerabilities require upstream patching.

threats.attack: WebUI starts another Pi runtime against the same session.
threats.residualRisk: Unsupported host APIs keep Chat/Control disabled.

threats.attack: A route or sidecar executes a filesystem/provider action without Pi guard.
threats.residualRisk: Trusted code outside observed tool paths retains OS authority.

threats.attack: A stale tab targets a replacement session, task or agent operation.
threats.residualRisk: Unknown identity disables the affected action.

threats.attack: Arbitrary path, traversal, symlink or opaque-ref confusion reads protected data.
threats.residualRisk: Same-account processes can read outside this application boundary.

threats.attack: A stale, replayed or racing approval authorizes a different action or later operation.
threats.residualRisk: Disconnect and ambiguity resolve to deny or terminal fallback.

threats.attack: Repository Git config launches a clean filter, hook, textconv, external diff, pager or recursive submodule process.
threats.residualRisk: The trusted repository may execute code through mechanisms outside WebUI collection.

threats.attack: Baseline, verifier, provenance or event persistence retains protected content or becomes cross-account readable.
threats.residualRisk: Backups and same-account processes remain outside the application boundary.

threats.attack: UI overclaims agent authorship, satisfied criteria, current verifier, running state or completion.
threats.residualRisk: Concurrent human writes may remain mixed or unattributed.

threats.attack: Corrupt, partial, symlinked or replaced local state is accepted as authority.
threats.residualRisk: Application integrity does not defend against a malicious same-account process.

threats.attack: Huge diffs, logs, event floods, slow clients or Git processes exhaust CPU, memory, file descriptors or event-loop time.
threats.residualRisk: A hostile trusted process can exhaust the OS outside WebUI limits.

threats.attack: Tool output, command arguments, filenames or logs expose credentials through previews or events.
threats.residualRisk: Novel or transformed secret formats can evade pattern redaction.

threats.attack: WebUI crash, restart, corrupt replay or disk failure interrupts the active Pi task.
threats.residualRisk: Terminal remains the required fallback surface.

threats.attack: A frontend dependency, CDN, analytics script or dynamic loader gains browser authority.
threats.residualRisk: Dependency audits are point-in-time and require continued maintenance.

threats.attack: A hostile client smuggles a path, spoofed type, oversized content or stale reference into another Pi message or session.
threats.residualRisk: A selected text attachment may intentionally contain hostile instructions; explicit Send remains the operator action.

threats.attack: A stale or cross-view browser intent marks source as reviewed without the operator seeing the exact current diff.
threats.residualRisk: Concurrent source changes reject or stale the review; they are never merged into the acknowledgement.

threats.attack: A stale preview, opaque-ref mixup or concurrent Git writer stages or unstages a different file/index image than the operator reviewed.
threats.residualRisk: Non-cooperating same-account processes can alter repository files outside the application boundary; postcondition ambiguity remains uncertain.

threats.attack: A stale, substituted or ambiguous confirmation discards source other than the exact unstaged file or hunk the operator previewed.
threats.residualRisk: A non-cooperating same-account writer can race the filesystem outside the application lock; an unprovable postcondition is reported uncertain.

threats.attack: A hostile browser or repository record substitutes a path, URI, executable, argument or stale opaque reference to launch an unintended local editor action or expose protected source.
threats.residualRisk: Visual Studio Code and same-account local processes remain outside Piagent isolation after the explicit handoff is accepted.

threats.attack: A stale index, hostile filename or hidden model path smuggles unstaged, protected or secret content into a commit summary or consumes model tokens without explicit operator acknowledgement.
threats.residualRisk: The advisory Pi-generated wording can still be imperfect and must be reviewed before the operator creates a commit.

threats.attack: A mutation is presented as settled without matching durable evidence, or stale review/verifier facts remain current after the exact source or index preimage changed.
threats.residualRisk: Verifier commands captured before per-file snapshots remain stale with invalidating files unknown rather than inferred.

threats.attack: Corrupt, stale or cross-session local state is merged by display text, leaks raw state identity, or is presented as a trusted active/recent task run.
threats.residualRisk: Legacy valid contracts can appear with reduced-evidence warnings until migrated; WUI4-07 adds full scale and retention stress gates.

threats.attack: A corrupt, gapped or cross-run journal, or an incomplete final write, is presented as a confirmed crash, resume, pause or checkpoint fact and misleads recovery decisions.
threats.residualRisk: Pi currently records no dedicated crash event, so crash remains unknown unless a recoverable incomplete tail provides only possible-interruption evidence.

threats.attack: Compaction history leaks retained tool or prompt content, capture paths, content hashes or raw session identity, or presents corrupt/cross-run telemetry as a complete history.
threats.residualRisk: Bounded telemetry rotation can omit older compaction facts; the UI reports partial or missing history and WUI4-07 adds scale and retention stress gates.

threats.attack: A cross-run, corrupt or stale handoff is shown as current, private handoff data leaks, or a displayed next action becomes hidden execution authority.
threats.residualRisk: Telemetry rotation may leave only the latest validated snapshot; the UI labels snapshot-only history and WUI4-07 stress-tests retention.

threats.attack: A corrupt or cross-run helper ledger is shown as a trusted ownership tree, a stale late result is presented as accepted, nested lineage is invented, or private helper authority and output metadata leak through the projection.
threats.residualRisk: The current durable ledger proves only direct task-to-helper ownership; deeper subagent lineage remains unavailable until runtime records it.

threats.attack: A corrupt, cross-project, stale or ledger-unbound benchmark or release report is presented as current quality evidence, leaks private run metadata, or gains authority to run a benchmark or perform a release action.
threats.residualRisk: Legacy benchmark reports without a durable ledger remain unavailable rather than being upgraded; release readiness remains advisory and never grants publish authority.

threats.attack: Rotated, truncated, oversized, symlinked or corrupt long-task evidence is read outside its authority boundary, shown as a complete current history, leaks private identity, or exhausts Pi and WebUI resources.
threats.residualRisk: Bounded retention can omit older valid history; the UI reports truncation or unavailability and never reconstructs missing facts from model prose.

threats.attack: Two local Gateways for one profile or two SDK runtimes acquire and write the same durable Pi session concurrently.
threats.residualRisk: A malicious same-account process can bypass application locks and remains outside Piagent containment.

threats.attack: PID reuse, missed heartbeat, stale browser authority or an unresponsive owner is treated as proof that a live terminal or Gateway session can be stolen.
threats.residualRisk: Unknown owner liveness intentionally leaves the session recovery-required until explicit reconciliation.

threats.attack: A terminal writes or starts work after release while the Gateway concurrently acquires the same session, or an old terminal epoch reconnects after handoff.
threats.residualRisk: Non-cooperating same-account runtimes require OS isolation beyond the application handoff protocol.

threats.attack: A crash, retry, corrupt journal or stale tab duplicates create, send or fork effects, loses accepted content, or reports an ambiguous effect as settled.
threats.residualRisk: Ambiguous dispatched work requires explicit recovery and may remain uncertain instead of being automatically repaired.

threats.attack: An allocated Pi session or fork path whose JSONL is deferred until the first assistant message is presented as a durable completed conversation.
threats.residualRisk: A pre-assistant crash can remain recovery-required when no exact no-effect proof is available.

threats.attack: Session title, preview, project label, model metadata, raw JSONL path or local identity leaks secrets through catalog pages or live events.
threats.residualRisk: Novel transformed secret formats can evade display redaction and require credential hygiene.
